sources.entry: Jitsi Video Bridge - WebRTC compatible Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) that allows for multiuser video communication. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/deb

summary.one_liner: Jitsi Videobridge is a WebRTC-compatible Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) that routes multimedia for multiuser video calls and serves as a backend component of the Jitsi Meet stack.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Jitsi Videobridge as a WebRTC-compatible SFU, meaning a multimedia router for multiuser video communication. It is one of the backend components in the Jitsi Meet stack. Binary packages are offered for Debian/Ubuntu in stable, testing, and nightly channels. Users can build a custom package with mvn install, which produces an archive in the jvb/target directory. For local runs, it can be started with Maven or from an IDE using a jvb.conf file in a user config directory. Runtime settings come from a config file (usually /etc/jitsi/videobridge/jvb.conf) that overrides defaults in reference.conf. On Debian, a separate config file sets JVM options such as max heap size and garbage collector type. The README points to further documentation in the doc/ directory and the Jitsi Meet Handbook.
use_cases: backend media routing for Jitsi Meet
running a self-hosted WebRTC video bridge
forwarding video streams between call participants
building a custom Jitsi Videobridge package
how_to_run: Install Debian/Ubuntu binary package from the stable, testing, or nightly channel (see README instructions)
Create ~/.jvb/jvb.conf to set environment and options (see reference.conf)
Run locally: mvn compile exec:exec with org.jitsi.videobridge.MainKt, as shown in the README
notable: WebRTC-compatible Selective Forwarding Unit, a backend component of Jitsi Meet
Debian/Ubuntu binary packages in stable, testing, and nightly channels
HOCON-style config file with defaults in reference.conf
Debian JVM tuning via /etc/jitsi/videobridge/config (heap size, GC type)
caveats: Designed as a backend component of the Jitsi Meet stack rather than a standalone app
README says GitHub issues are only for actionable items; questions go to the Jitsi Community Forum
Local run requires Maven and manual configuration of paths and config files
